title: GitLab Vulnerability Under Active Exploitation Enables Unauthenticated Data Exfiltration
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/gitlab-critical-vulnerabilities/en/headerimage/gitlab-cloud-seed-preview-1791042234130.jpeg"/><p>CVE-2026-85706 is a critical GitLab path-traversal vulnerability that has moved beyond theoretical risk into confirmed exploitation. It affects self-managed GitLab CE/EE and could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to read arbitrary files from the GitLab.</p> <i>By Sergio De Simone</i>

title: Presentation: Building GenAI Platform at DoorDash
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/doordash-genai-platform-architecture/en/mediumimage/SiddharthKodwaniSwaroopChitlur-medium-1790246592519.jpg"/><p>Swaroop Chitlur and Sidd Kodwani share DoorDash’s journey building an internal GenAI platform. They discuss core architectural bets, transitioning from vendor-first setups to open-weights models, navigating LLM and agent gateways, and balancing accuracy, latency, and cost for over 5,000 internal users.</p> <i>By Siddharth Kodwani, Swaroop Chitlur</i>

title: Istio 1.31 Adds Agentgateway Waypoints and Moves Release Artifacts off Google Cloud
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/istio-1-31-agentgateway/en/headerimage/header-1790887193946.jpeg"/><p>Istio 1.31 adds agentgateway waypoints in ambient mode, with a canary configuration fix included in 1.31.1. It also ends the publication of images and Helm charts to Google Cloud, requiring repository migration ahead of the 13 October outage test and signing-key updates for teams verifying images.</p> <i>By Mark Silvester</i>

title: AI Agents Are Disrupting Open Source Security Disclosure
partialText: <img src="https://www.infoq.com/styles/static/images/logo/logo_bigger.jpg"/><p>A recent article by Anil Madhavapeddy argues that AI agents can turn publicly available clues about software vulnerabilities into working exploits, reducing the effectiveness of traditional disclosure embargoes in open source projects. The author highlights the need for faster patching and release processes as the time between vulnerability disclosure and exploitation shrinks.</p> <i>By Renato Losio</i>

title: Uber Eats Rebuilds Search Pipeline to Cut End-to-End Latency by 50%
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/uber-eats-search-latency/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1789856971928.jpg"/><p>Uber has rebuilt major parts of the Uber Eats search pipeline, reporting a 50% reduction in end-to-end latency. Changes include Above-the-Fold measurement, reduced retrieval work, parallel hydration, advertising data redesign, infrastructure optimizations, and an agentic coding workflow. Uber is also exploring microbatching, product-based retrieval, and HTTP multipart streaming.</p> <i>By Leela Kumili</i>

title: Envoy Gateway 1.9.1 Tightens Security and Addresses a Difficult Upgrade Path
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/envoy-gateway-1-9-1/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1790172096430.jpg"/><p>Envoy Gateway has released v1.9.1, a maintenance release that focuses heavily on security, upgrade reliability, and operational correctness following the broader v1.9 release.</p> <i>By Craig Risi</i>

title: Presentation: Managing Asynchronous APIs at Scale
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/managing-async-apis/en/mediumimage/ian-cooper-medium-1790242149604.jpeg"/><p>Ian Cooper discusses managing asynchronous APIs in event-driven architectures at scale. He explains the "ABCs" of messaging (Address, Binding, Contract) and shares how to tackle discovery, governance, and provisioning using AsyncAPI, CloudEvents, schema registries, and automated CI/CD infrastructure pipelines based on real-world engineering practices at Just Eat Takeaway.</p> <i>By Ian Cooper</i>

title: OpenAI DevDay 2026 Recap for Developers
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/openai-devday-2026/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1790873120154.jpg"/><p>OpenAI announced a series of product and developer updates at DevDay 2026, including GPT-6.1 Sol, computer use for the Agents API, cloud-based Codex environments, a Decisions API, and new plugin capabilities for ChatGPT.</p> <i>By Daniel Dominguez</i>

title: Engineering Production Systems for an Agentic Era: QCon San Francisco 2026
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/qconsf-2026-sessions/en/headerimage/qcon-sf-2026-session-focus-1790849488514.jpg"/><p>QCon San Francisco 2026 will bring together practitioners from Airbnb, OpenAI, Netflix, Honeycomb, and other engineering organizations to share how they are building, operating, and evolving production systems as AI agents take on a larger role.</p> <i>By Artenisa Chatziou</i>

title: Article: From Reusable to Regeneratable: Rethinking the Shared UI Component Library
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/articles/regeneratable-ui-component-library/en/headerimage/regeneratable-ui-component-library-header-1790758478325.jpg"/><p>Regeneration has changed reuse economics. A model pointed at a solid design system can produce most standard UI on demand, so paying to keep a canonical component package alive is much harder to justify than it used to be. Keep the design system, tokens, guidelines and tests central. They are what actually buy you consistency.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

title: Docker Sandbox Kit Spec: Packaging AI Agent Permissions as OCI Images
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/docker-sandbox-ai-agent/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1790838829021.jpg"/><p>Docker has announced that it is bringing the Sandbox Kit Specification to the CNCF, aiming to make what an AI agent may access as portable as the agent itself.</p> <i>By Claudio Masolo</i>

title: DigitalOcean Managed Agents Brings Managed Cloud Infrastructure to AI Agents
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/digitalocean-managed-agents/en/headerimage/digitalocean-managed-agents-1790930999544.jpeg"/><p>DigitalOcean recently launched DigitalOcean Managed Agents in public preview, offering a managed cloud infrastructure layer for AI agents with isolated microVM runtimes, governed tool access, and serverless AI inference.</p> <i>By Sergio De Simone</i>

title: Qualcomm Unveils Linux Preview on Snapdragon X2 to Accelerate Upstream ARM Laptops
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/snapdragon-x2-linux/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1790506107899.jpg"/><p>Qualcomm has released an early dev preview of Linux for its upcoming Snapdragon X2 Series laptop processors. The initiative focuses on integrating with the mainline Linux kernel ahead of commercial release to reduce software issues historically faced by ARM laptops. The preview includes a functional Debian 13 environment and aims to standardize system initialization and hardware task management.</p> <i>By Olimpiu Pop</i>

title: Presentation: Beyond Observability: Evolving Production Operations in the Age of AI
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/ai-production-operations/en/mediumimage/infoq-live-medium-1790856304338.jpg"/><p>The panelists discuss how production operations are evolving with AI, turning operational data into actionable insights for incident response. They explain how automation and new architectural practices help engineering teams build more understandable systems, while exploring how AI reshapes software delivery and changes the historically deterministic nature of production applications.</p> <i>By Michael Hausenblas, Sujana Sooreddy, Noam Levi, Renato Losio</i>

title: How to Develop Software Engineering Skills in the Age of AI
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/software-engineering-skills/en/headerimage/header-1790604007454.jpg"/><p>Software engineering skill development requires slowing down. Generative AI has changed the landscape of skill development for software engineering. Tools and AI can accelerate outcomes, but they may not support skill development. Engineers must understand how systems work to learn things. Senior developers can coach juniors by using learning techniques.</p> <i>By Ben Linders</i>
